La coronaria destra si vede bene nelle p:
The right coronary artery is well seen in the left anterior oblique projections ("C"-shaped course) and in the right one ("L"-shaped course): here in all three sequences there is a tight narrowing of the distal segment, near the crux, where the posterior descending artery and the posterolateral branch arise. A lesion like this (90-98%), in a patient with NSTEMI, is the most likely candidate for the culprit and is treated with angioplasty and stenting.
Estimating the stenosis: compare the minimum diameter with the neighboring healthy segment, in at least two projections. The proximal stenosis is mild-to-moderate in most projections: the only projection that makes it look more severe may be due to foreshortening or overlap, so it is assessed on several views (and, in doubtful cases, with FFR).
Pitfalls: catheter spasm at the ostium of the right coronary artery; an overlapping right ventricular branch simulating a stenosis; cardiac motion blurring the frames (choose the end-diastolic one, with the vessel still and well opacified).
Ogni stenosi si giudica in almeno due pr: Every stenosis is judged in at least two projections, on the frame with the vessel still and full of contrast.
